notes:
The Department of Public Works Bureau of Engineering Photograph Records read whole — 984 catalogue records, all `No Copyright – United States`. 946 give no street number and are skipped: sewer trenches, pump houses, water towers, street grading and reservoir work, located by intersection rather than by number. 20 addressed records became 17 findings.

**Five findings exist because the Bureau writes a run of buildings with a word between the numbers.** "610 to 624 Anza Street", "183 to 94 Cook Street", "169 to 73 Cook Street", "170 to 196 Cook Street" — a pattern that knows only the hyphen matched the *second* number and filed the photograph on it, silently losing the first, and on the Cook Street rows that second number was an abbreviated high end read literally: 94 for 194, 73 for 173. Each run is now read as the two numbers the caption prints, one finding each, per "A row of buildings is not a range" in research/AGENTS.md, with the short high end filled in from the low. `extra.address_as_printed` keeps the caption's own words on both.

**12 resolved, and 5 of those were declined on the roll year.** The Bureau photographed these properties in 1935–1942 and five of the parcels carry something much newer: 624 Anza Street (roll 1972), 170 Cook Street (1987), 1515 3rd Street (2021), 230 Dolores Street (1960), and 1648–1650 3rd Street, which resolves onto a Mission Bay superblock the assessor files as 555 Mission Bay Boulevard and which carries 1450, 1560, 1650 and 1750 3rd Street on one lot. Seven were published.

**One resolution was wrong and the tool now raises the shape.** 1458 Kirkwood Avenue is in EAS with coordinates and no parcel number, and the one active parcel its point falls in states its own range as 1470–1498 Kirkwood — it is the neighbour. `resolve_eas.py report` now prints every point-placed resolution whose parcel's stated range excludes the number, sorted by how far outside it falls. It raises rather than decides: measured over every findings file in the repo the test fires on 61 of 582 point-placed resolutions and most of those are correct, because sf-parcels' `from_address_num`/`to_address_num` is routinely narrower than the EAS numbers a parcel actually holds.

The remaining four unresolved are addresses EAS no longer has (194 and 196 Cook Street, 433 Seventh Avenue), one that EAS holds without a parcel join (610 Anza Street), and one condominium (173 Cook Street).

coverage.note: Read every record in the collection: 984 unique catalogue records, 20 of which give a street number, becoming 17 findings over 17 distinct addresses once the four "N to M Street" runs are split into one finding per printed number. 12 resolved, 7 published on 6 pages seeded for them, 5 declined on a roll year decades after the photograph. 5 unresolved: three addresses EAS no longer holds, one EAS holds without a parcel join, one condominium.

findings.description: The San Francisco Department of Public Works Bureau of Engineering photographed the property at 1648 - 50 3rd Street on 1941-02-17.

corporate_subject_headings: San Francisco Department of Public Works (San Francisco, Calif.)

citation.label: 1648 - 50 3rd Street, 1941. San Francisco Department of Public Works Bureau of Engineering Photograph Records (SFP 26), San Francisco History Center, San Francisco Public Library.

resolution.method: Recorded range 1648-50 03RD ST; EAS matches 1650 on this street → parcel 8711509; sf-parcels has blklot 8711509 active; the 2025 roll records it as commercial office. The assessor files the parcel as 555 MISSION BAY BL. EAS puts 1450, 1560, 1650, 1750 03RD ST on that parcel, so per the directory contract the fact belongs on one page at the lowest, 1450. EAS files the address under parcel 8711007, which sf-parcels reports retired; the active parcel its coordinates fall in is 8711509. EAS has no record for 1648 on this street.
resolution.note: No page at this path yet; the parcel is the publisher's to seed.

publish.note: Resolved onto parcel 8711509, which the assessor files as 555 Mission Bay Boulevard, records as commercial office, and which carries 1450, 1560, 1650 and 1750 03RD ST together — a Mission Bay superblock built long after 1941. EAS has no 1648 at all. Publishing here would hang a 1941 photograph of two industrial addresses on a building that replaced the whole block.
